# `scope_set_time`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Set the date, time and zone offset on the connected mount.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build matches (READ)) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, guider handler @0x7b540, ScopeAM5::SetTime, Utc2Local, SetTimeCmd (64-bit build) |

Calls the mount time setter, which issues time commands to the mount. Requires a connected mount that supports time setting. utc must contain a YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS date-time (trailing text tolerated); offset is the zone offset in hours, fractions allowed, positive east of UTC (sign INFERRED). The driver converts the pair to local date and time and sends offset, date and time to the mount; a year whose last two digits are 21 or less fails with 207. Does not change the host clock or zone. Via the imager command port (4700) the request reaches this handler only as a forwarded unknown method; see the control service for the relay. Mount serial (firmware 9.31, READ): :SG, :SC, :SL in that order.

Side effects: Changes the mount clock and zone offset.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"scope_set_time"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object\|array | yes | - | Object with offset and utc strings, or the positional array [offset, utc]. Both are required strings. The handler applies no lexical check; the mount driver parses both, converts the pair to local date and time and sends the zone offset, date and time to the mount. A year whose last two digits are 21 or less is rejected (207). [READ] |
| `params.offset` | string | yes | - | Zone offset in hours, positive east of UTC ("8" for UTC+8); fractions are allowed and are sent to the mount as minutes. The local date and time are computed with the integer hours. [READ (syntax); INFERRED (east-positive sign, from the mount command's convention)] |
| `params.utc` | string | yes | - | UTC date-time text that must contain YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS. It is found by search, not an anchored match, so trailing text such as Z or a fraction is tolerated. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | offset or utc missing or not a string | `expected string param` |
| 207 | Native setter failure, including a year whose last two digits are 21 or less | `fail to operate` |
| 210 | Mount does not support setting the time | `not supported` |
| 315 | No mount connected | `mount is not connected` |
| 209 | Two-digit year of 21 or less (the driver refuses to set the year) | `invalid value` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request is not an object, is an empty object, or has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: no method of type string (a non-string method counts as missing) | `invalid request` |
| 101 | Dispatcher: text fails to parse | `invalid JSON request: <reason> on line <n> ...` |
| 103 | Dispatcher: unregistered method | `method not found` |

## Example

Request, request - Example request (values invented):

```json
{"id":45,"method":"scope_set_time","params":{"offset":"1","utc":"2026-01-31T20:15:00Z"}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_set_time","result":0,"code":0,"id":45}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_set_time","error":"expected string param","code":105,"id":46}
```
